newsitem.title: USA: IMM currency futures close mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: IMM currency futures close mostly higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed mostly higher, with yen ending off its lows after Japanese Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said he supports a "strong" dollar, not a stronger dollar, traders and analysts said.

December yen bounced above $0.009075, as the dollar/yen stabilized around the 111.40 spot level. They said offers emerged around the 111.70 spot level after Kubo's comments and lifted December yen off the bottom of its range. The 111.70 area is roughly equivalent to the contract low of $0.009049.
"It's going to be a grind up for the dollar now," one trader said.
Some traders said December yen could test $0.009043, or 111.80 spot in the near-term.
"People still want to buy on dollar dips," one trader said. "I have the suspicion that the market is not completely long."

Likewise, December marks are expected to continue to weaken in the near term, despite light central bank selling of dollar/marks this afternoon, traders said. The dollar selling, as well as some options-related buying in both marks and Swiss francs, helped bring December above its four-month low at $0.6577 and kept December Swiss francs in positive territory.

"The dollar has been strong since the end of July," one trader said. "There is probably more strength there." Support for December marks is at $0.6535, which is now equivalent to the dollar/mark's four-month high set on June 10 at 1.5383.
Most traders believe December marks will test $0.6490, which would be a contract low, as the dollar seems poised for a re-test of the year-and-a-half high at 1.5488 spot.
Nina Cooper, president of Pendragon Research, believes the dollar/mark will test the top from late May in the near term, but that the upside is limited.
"I think it will run out of steam," Cooper said. "I would be scaling back positions. I would not be a buyer at these levels. You will have time later in the year to get long dollars."
According to Elliott Wave price patterns, the dollar's strength is corrective, she said.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was down $0.000042 at $0.009076, marks were down $0.0004 at $0.6590, Swiss francs were up $0.0013 at $0.8039, sterling was up $0.0012 at $1.5646, Canadian dollars were up $0.0005 at $0.7366, Australian dollars were up $0.0005 at $0.7889.
